methodology: News items gathered via Brave Search API (8 queries, EN + 繁體中文) and full-text reading of key reporting: HKFP timeline (2025-12-17), HKFP first-10-days hearing findings (2026-04-12), HKFP closing-address report (2026-07-17), The Standard reforms piece (2026-05-12). 65 unique articles identified across international and Hong Kong media. Themes are mapped to the Committee's Terms of Reference; the same events appear in the inquiry documents available on this site.

fire_facts.estate: Wang Fuk Court (宏福苑), Tai Po — completed 1983 under the Home Ownership Scheme; 8 blocks, 31 storeys each; ~2,000 flats; ~4,600 residents (2021 census)
fire_facts.fire_date: 2025-11-26, 14:51 FSD alerted; escalated No.3 15:02, No.4 15:34, No.5 18:22; under control ~15:00 next day; extinguished 10:18 28 Nov (43+ hours)
fire_facts.death_toll: 168 killed (incl. one firefighter) per committee closing address; earlier official figures: 160+ (9 Dec 2025), 6 unaccounted at that time
fire_facts.renovation: HK$330M renovation (2016 Mandatory Building Inspection order; Will Power Architects consultancy; Prestige Construction main contractor; works began July 2024; household levy HK$160k-180k)
fire_facts.cause: Committee counsel: lit cigarette on flat roof of light well outside flats 104-105, Wang Cheong House, ignited combustible cartons (based on govt laboratory + Fire Investigation Task Force preliminary report)

timeline.event: Mandatory Building Inspection Scheme order issued to Wang Fuk Court owners' corporation
Will Power Architects awarded inspection project
Will Power chosen to supervise the repair works
Three renovation plans proposed; most extensive ~HK$300M
595 owners/authorised reps (30% of shareholders) vote; most expensive plan chosen; Prestige Construction appointed; cost rises to HK$330M
Renovation begins: bamboo scaffolding, protective netting, foam boards over windows; residents complain of fire hazards
Photo of cigarette butt on exterior wall posted; residents urge contractor supervision of smoking workers
Photos of burning foam board; residents oust owners' committee; Labour Department complaint filed
ICU (Housing Bureau) test reports find 'no non-compliance' / 'no combustible' features in netting; Labour Dept replies to complaints
Labour Dept inspects 16 times, issues 6 improvement notices, 3 prosecutions (fines up to HK$18,000); last inspection 20 Nov 2025 — six days before the fire
Fire at 14:51; 7 of 8 blocks ablaze; firefighter Ho Wai-ho dies; death toll climbs 4→13→36→55→128 across two days
Police arrest 3 Prestige directors/consultant on suspicion of manslaughter; CE John Lee: 36 dead, 279 missing
ICAC arrests 8 incl. 2 Will Power directors; 7 of 20 netting samples fail fire-safety tests; substandard netting + foam boards blamed for rapid spread
13→15 arrests for manslaughter; CE Lee: 'systemic issues' — 'inappropriate connected interests, conflicts of roles and corrupt collusion'; judge-led independent review committee announced
High Court Judge David Lok appointed to lead Independent Committee; 9-month reporting window
Public hearings begin; cause: likely lit cigarette; 168 deaths confirmed

First-10-days findings: alarms off (unqualified electrician), foam boards brushed off, FSD 'standard procedure' inspection missed deactivated systems, 85 shutdown-renewal notices, proxy-vote irregularities
Fourth round (24 hearings, 77 witnesses) concludes; govt pre-emptively rolls out 6-point reform plan; Lok: no confirmed citywide bid-rigging pattern yet

Closing submissions: 627-page address; 'continuous fraud, bad materials, false certificates, blatant lying'; govt has 'unshirkable responsibility'; hearings close; committee continues processing evidence

themes.title: Cause of fire: smoking on renovation works
themes.coverage: Committee counsel identified a lit cigarette on the light-well roof as the probable ignition source; CCTV showed workers smoking on the day of the fire. Media repeatedly connected the cause to supervision failures at the renovation site.
media: 星島 2026-08-08 '宏福苑大火或由煙頭引起'
themes.gaps: Witness statements and lab reports on ignition sequencing are in the documents; media has not shown the light-well layout or carton storage chain as clearly as the Committee's own exhibits.

themes.title: Disabled fire alarms, hydrants and hose reels
themes.coverage: An unqualified electrician (ISS EastPoint) switched off main power in all 8 blocks to empty fire water tanks; fire alarms did not sound; hoses did not work; fire-safety contractors (Victory Fire, China Status) were unaware or did not follow up; 85 shutdown-renewal notices submitted without site visits.
media: SCMP 'Tai Po fire: corrupt players exploited loopholes'
themes.gaps: Media rarely explains the FSD shutdown-notification regime in detail; the notice trail is fully visible in the inquiry documents (China Status statements).

themes.title: Flammable foam boards and non-retardant netting
themes.coverage: Styrofoam boards over windows fuelled fire spread and blocked residents' views; non-fire-retardant nets replaced typhoon-damaged nets (Prestige + Gain Profit); ICU classified boards 'temporary' despite a year of use; govt later banned combustible exterior materials.
media: NBC 'Substandard work and evasion of oversight'
themes.gaps: Material test reports and ICU correspondence are primary sources media cites but rarely publishes in full.

themes.title: Supervision vacuum: rubber-stamp inspectors and contractors
themes.coverage: Registered inspector for Will Power and China Status 'acted as mere rubber stamps'; management company had 'limited power'; unclear which department enforces no-smoking rules; FSD inspection 5 weeks before fire missed deactivated alarms; ICU advance notices let Prestige prepare for checks.
media: SCMP 'missed checks at Wang Fuk Court'
themes.gaps: The precise statutory duties of each regulator vs the honour system are under-explained in most coverage; the documents contain the department-by-department statements.

themes.title: Collusion, bid-rigging and proxy votes
themes.coverage: ICAC arrests over renovation corruption; 'inappropriate connected interests, conflicts of roles and corrupt collusion' (CE Lee); abnormal tender prices; pervasive unauthorised proxy votes at owners' meetings (>50% proxies typical); DAB district councillor was consultant to owners' corporation 2021-24.
themes.gaps: Competition Commission material and tender documents are on the Committee site; media coverage is arrest-led, not document-led.

themes.title: Adequacy of laws, penalties and the honour system
themes.coverage: 'Honour system' of self-regulation 'effectively leaving them without oversight' (Dawes); fines as low as HK$18,000 for safety breaches; unclear jurisdiction over construction-site smoking; cladding regulations inapplicable to 'temporary' boards.
themes.gaps: Most coverage quotes the problem; the Committee documents contain the actual statutes, codes and penalty schedules to evaluate it.

themes.title: Reforms and recommendations
themes.coverage: Govt 6-point pre-emptive reform: 4-monthly inspections for large projects, tech-driven random audits, mandatory supervision plans + prosecution for negligence, material testing + ban on combustible exteriors, phased construction for multi-block estates, inter-departmental collaboration. Dawes: widen URA Smart Tender Scheme, compulsory litigation-record disclosure, proxy-vote reform. Hearings closed 17 Jul 2026; final report pending.
media: The Standard 2026-07-22 'reforms ahead of final report'
themes.gaps: None of the pre-emptive reforms had been stress-tested publicly against the Committee's actual recommendations at time of writing — a live question for the final report.

coverage_gaps: No dedicated data-driven explainer that links each news claim to the underlying inquiry document (this site's purpose).
Light-well ignition sequence and carton storage chain shown in Committee exhibits rarely reproduced with page-level citations.
FSD shutdown-notification regime (14-day renewals, 85 notices) under-explained in general coverage.
The ICU 'temporary use' classification of foam boards is mostly mentioned in passing; the correspondence trail is in the documents.
Proxy-vote irregularities are reported but not connected to the wider owners' corporation decision trail (tender approvals).
Chinese-language coverage lags on the technical expert reports (Usmani/Jiang fire engineering) that anchor the cause narrative.
insights: The seven ToR categories map 1:1 onto the news themes — meaning the Committee's own structure is the missing navigation layer for the public record.

News coverage is event-led (arrests, hearings); the documentary record is richer than any single report — e.g. the 85-notice shutdown trail and ICU correspondence are primary evidence that only the Committee site publishes.
The 'honour system' critique recurs across departments (ICU, FSD, BD, Labour) — a systemic thread that cuts across ToR4/ToR6 and is best shown by reading department statements side by side.

Fire-safety contractor behaviour (rubber-stamping, no site visits) is a distinct pattern from the renovation contractor fraud — two parallel failure chains that meet in the disabled fire systems (ToR2).
Smoking-caused fires on renovation sites: the Wang Fuk case is likely not unique; the documents may support a systemic-risk argument for the final report.

latest_developments.event: Government rules out extending the buy-back deadline (31 Aug) as ~100 owners have yet to accept; compensation may fall if flats are acquired by legal means.
Government still weighing whether to restrict proxy voting at owners' meetings - a reform gap the inquiry evidence highlighted.
Our letter on the accessibility of the inquiry documents is published in SCMP Letters - see the Our Letter page.
The Committee's final report is delayed until the end of October; it will present its findings and recommendations after the hearings that closed on 17 July.
Inquiry documents show supplier Gain Profit ordered non-fire-retardant netting before the blaze; lawmakers flag gaps in the proposed building-management rules.
Committee releases the task force's interim report on the death of firefighter Ho Wai-ho, including images of his gear.
Labour Department begins testing thermal drones to catch illegal smoking at construction sites; AI added later.
SCMP investigation finds two fire-service contractors linked to the tragedy (China Status, Victory Fire) are still in business and taking new contracts.
Two contractor directors deny all allegations in witness statements published by the inquiry.
Competition watchdog tightens tender clauses to target bid-rigging - bidders must sign statutory declarations against collusion.
Final report delayed to late October; the committee needs more time to organise the evidence.
